provenance: 5G-NIDD: real traffic from a 5G test network at the University of Oulu, as flow statistics. This is the network layer, a different task from the QKD-layer attacks the other model on this page classifies, with no feature in common.
split_note: 4,096 rows from the published evaluation sample, a per-class-floored draw of the held-out quarter of the seed-42 stratified split: none was used to fit telecom_ids.nidd. The floor over-represents the rare attacks, so the base rate here is the sample's and not the corpus's.
attribution: Y. Siriwardhana et al., 'Descriptor: 5G Wireless Network Intrusion Detection Dataset (5G-NIDD)', in IEEE Data Descriptions, doi:10.1109/IEEEDATA.2025.3592888. Dataset: doi:10.23729/e80ac9df-d9fb-47e7-8d0d-01384a415361, CC BY 4.0.
modifications: Two of the 113 columns, rounded to 4 significant figures, on 4,096 rows of a stratified held-out draw; the 8 attack classes collapsed to attack against benign.

x.label: mean packet size from the source (bytes)

separability_method: 5-fold cross-validated two-feature random forest over these points
note: AUC-PR 0.8707 against a 0.636 base rate. Most of the attacks stand apart and much of the benign traffic does not: UDPFlood sits on top of it, which is where this model's errors are. The model reads 46 columns and scores accuracy 0.7616 over 9 classes, Benign and UDPFlood being the only pair it confuses; two columns are enough to show that pair overlapping and not enough to score the model.
